newsitem.title: USA: Maine gets emergency aid due floods,NH still waits.
newsitem.headline: Maine gets emergency aid due floods,NH still waits.

text.p: Maine said that it was granted emergency federal aid for its two southernmost counties, which were blasted by a powerful northeaster that ran up the coast, though New Hampshire still is waiting for Washington's ruling.

The emergency declaration for Maine, which was released late Thursday, means it will get funds for temporary housing, debris removal, and various emergency services. It mirrors a decision by President Bill Clinton on Wednesday to give Massachusetts the same aid for five of its eastern counties.
Though the storm had no name, the severe floods it caused also hurt New Hampshire, which still is waiting to hear whether Clinton will grant it the emergency relief.
The three New England states also are hoping to qualify for the much bigger package of relief they would get if the president declared the communities that were hit to be major disaster areas.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency said it still is doing assessments of the damage and a spokeswoman declined to say when the work would finish and a decision on a major disaster declaration would be made. "Until all the information is gathered and analyzed there won't be a decision," said Karen Grossman, a spokeswoman for the agency.
Maine's officials were a bit more optimistic about the timing of the president's decision, saying they expected Clinton to act as soon as Friday.

Both Maine and Massachusetts officials have said they are confident their states will qualify as major disaster areas, entitling them to get both public assistance, to rebuild their infrastructure, and aid for individuals, such as grants and low-interest loans for homes and businesses.
